steps.title: Webots rover simulation environment
steps.summary: Connected the existing rover architecture to a Webots Mars desert environment using a custom URDF and world file with realistic obstacles, used a ROS bridge to connect the architecture to Webots, and simulated 14 rover software modules including object detection, obstacle avoidance, autonomous driving, and manual control.

steps.title: RTK GPS and heading accuracy work
steps.summary: Improved rover positioning to 99.8% accuracy by combining satellite GPS with real-time 10 Hz RTCM correction, worked with the RTK GPS module and initially connected it through ArduPilot Pixhawk configuration, and integrated an OakD IMU with custom EKF filtering to improve compass heading accuracy.

steps.title: Fast perception stack for rover vision
steps.summary: Replaced slow camera-plus-CPU detection with a faster OakD plus NPU plus ROS pipeline for real-time inference, built custom-trained YOLOv6 models, and detected mallets, hammers, and ARUCO tags with a more responsive pipeline.

steps.title: Theta* path planning over PointCloud2
steps.summary: Rewrote the rover avoidance algorithm from BFS to Theta* using PointCloud2 data, reduced rover latency by 70%, and improved avoidance efficiency significantly in constrained terrain.

steps.title: Assay analysis and embedded tests
steps.summary: Wrote algorithms to retrieve experimental data from Nile Red and Bradford assay outputs, smooth graphs, detect signs of life, and build tests for motor control and alignment algorithms used for carousel movement.

steps.title: Developer workflow and ROS2 migration
steps.summary: Created a Docker container used by the 20+ member software team and served as a primary contributor to the ROS to ROS2 switch, increasing package range and capabilities.

title: Fruit Fly Connectome RNN
points: PyTorch RNN with weights initialized from the fruit fly connectome (neuPrint)
Models the T4/T5 circuit that detects motion direction
Training sat at chance (~50%): identical left/right weights trapped the optimizer
Randomized initialization broke the symmetry and reached 75% accuracy
lead: Took a connectome-constrained RNN from chance to 75% accuracy.
bullets: Built a recurrent neural network in PyTorch constrained by real Drosophila connectome data (Janelia neuPrint), modeling the biological T4/T5 motion-detection circuit.
Improved direction-classification accuracy from chance level (~50%) to ~75% by diagnosing and resolving training failures in the recurrent architecture.
Identified a symmetry-breaking bug where identical left/right weight initialization created a stable optimization dead-end, unlocking above-chance learning via randomized init.

images.caption: Motion-detection circuit connectivity (edge width = strength, green = excitatory, red = inhibitory)
Sampled skeletons of the motion-detection circuit neurons

title: ML From Scratch (C++)
bullets: Developed linear regression, binary logistic regression, and multiclass (softmax) logistic regression algorithms from scratch in C++; additionally implemented train-test split, matrix operations, & mini-batch gradient descent.
Achieved 90-100% accuracy on Iris/MNIST classification and an RMSE of $69K on California Housing dataset, in-line with standard baselines for these benchmarks.
Identified a per-operation memory allocation bottleneck in the matrix class, fixing it for a 22-38% runtime reduction across benchmarks.

title: LLM Fine-Tuning Efficiency
lead: Team of 4 (CSE 151B): lowest perplexity from 20 minutes of fine-tuning on a T4.
points: Built FP16 mixed precision and a warmup + cosine LR that decays over the time budget
Length-sorted, pre-tokenized batches: 2.9× more real tokens than the supplied loop
Validation perplexity 3.145 → 3.061 (−2.7%); hard-token loss down 1.7%
Ran the baseline comparisons: higher LR, larger batch, every story padded to 384
Benchmark: loss on the 10% of tokens the base model found hardest (6,852 positions)
Ablations: the speedups drove most of the gain; LR decay only helped at 20 minutes
description: Team project for CSE 151B: fine-tuned TinyStories-33M for the lowest held-out perplexity in a 20-minute Colab T4 budget. Added FP16 autocast, length-sorted pre-tokenized batches and a warmup + cosine learning-rate schedule over the time budget, processing 2.9x more real tokens than the supplied loop and lowering validation perplexity from 3.145 to 3.061. Evaluated with the team's hard-token benchmark: loss on the 10% of positions the base model found hardest.

title: Climate Projections
points: D3.js map and 3D globe of historical and projected tropical storm tracks
Compares storm behavior across CMIP6 climate scenarios
Time-series and statistical charts put past and present trends in context
Owned the visual design and story arc of the scrollytelling site
description: Built interactive map and 3D globe visualizations in D3.js to display historical and projected tropical storm tracks across multiple CMIP6 climate scenarios, enabling spatial comparison of storm behavior over time. Developed supplementary time-series and statistical charts contextualizing past and present storm trends, translating raw climate model ensemble data into clear, audience-readable graphics. Owned end-to-end visual design and narrative structure of a data-driven scrollytelling experience, ensuring cohesive styling and a guided story arc from historical context through future emissions projections.

title: Hantavirus Modeling
points: Joined 10K synthetic patient records with epidemiology, climate and World Bank data
A logistic-regression baseline without the added data caught only 18% of deaths
Cross-validated and grid-searched LR, random forest, XGBoost and LightGBM
Calibrated LightGBM with an F2/MCC-tuned threshold (0.12) reached F2 = 0.60
McNemar and Cochran's Q: tree models beat the baseline (p < 0.001)
SHAP explanations served in a Streamlit demo
lead: Built a three-stage pipeline to predict hantavirus deaths.
description: Implemented data cleaning pipelines and feature development for synthetic hantavirus clinical data, incorporating country-based epidemiological information, environmental data, and social metrics sourced from the Open-Meteo and World Bank APIs. Developed and tested a three-stage modeling pipeline for hantavirus mortality prediction, performing baseline classification, hyperparameter tuning, class calibration, and custom threshold tuning across Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Conducted secondary statistical analysis using McNemar Tests and Cochran's Q Test, and provided interpretation of top predictive features using SHAP.

title: Hotel Booking Analysis
points: Logistic regression on cancellations, controlling for lead time
Non-refundable deposits: 287× the odds of cancelling (refundable: 0.57×)
That near-perfect rate looks like a recording artifact, not real behavior
Linear model: segment × hotel beat hotel-only on nightly rate (partial F-test)
Resorts price below city hotels in most segments, down to −€26 for corporate
Residual diagnostics: all four linear-model assumptions were violated
lead: Fit two regressions in R on 119K hotel bookings.
description: Modeled 119K hotel bookings with logistic regression in R to predict cancellations and analyze pricing, finding that non-refundable deposits carry 287x higher cancellation odds. Tested model significance through hypothesis testing and ANOVA, and diagnosed linearity and normality assumptions via residual analysis.

title: Power Outage Prediction
points: Decision tree and random forest on 1,534 outages with 10+ climate/geo features
k-fold CV and GridSearchCV lifted accuracy from 57.9% to 69.4%
Engineered seasonal encoding and hurricane flags; cut multicollinearity
Median and probabilistic imputation for missing values
Permutation tests, TVD missingness analysis and subgroup fairness checks
description: Trained Decision Tree & Random Forest models on 1,534 outages with 10+ climate/geospatial features using k-fold CV & GridSearchCV, improving accuracy from 57.9% → 69.4% (+11.5%). Engineered custom features including seasonal encoding, hurricane binarization, multicollinearity reduction, & applied encoding with median & probabilistic imputation. Performed EDA, permutation testing, & missingness analysis using TVD-based statistics, validating effects on outage duration & fairness via subgroup accuracy testing.

title: Aletheia
points: Medical-aid and pill-tracking agentic AI app, built at CalHacks AI 2025
Letta agents on Claude 4 with drug-lookup and web-search tools
Insurance grading and pill-label reading with the Gemini API
description: Medical aid and pill tracking agentic AI web app, built at CalHacks AI 2025. Developed structured agentic AIs using Letta and Anthropic Claude 4, equipped with custom tools such as drug querying and web search, for personalized user recommendations regarding medicinal questions. Created inference models for insurance company grading and image detection models for label reading with Gemini Generative AI API.

title: TallyUp
points: Club finance app with nested groups, built at LA Hacks 2025
MERN backend from scratch with a React Native frontend
MongoDB nested documents for groups, subgroups and per-user balances
Express REST APIs for real-time debt tracking and ledger sync
description: Hierarchical club finance tracking app, built at LA Hacks 2025. Built backend from scratch using the MERN stack with React Native frontend; modeled nested groups, subgroups, and per-user balances using MongoDB with relational object structures and nested document design. Engineered RESTful APIs with Express and Axios for real-time debt tracking, custom member assignments, and ledger sync across recursive group trees; tackled bi-directional state-sharing logic between users and nested club structures.

title: ML Paper Recommender
points: Search for arXiv papers by abstract
TF-IDF vectors ranked by cosine similarity
description: Used queried ArXIV dataset, TF-IDF vectorization, and cosine similarity to return top search results for scientific papers based on abstract.

title: Airline Satisfaction
points: EDA and visualizations of multidimensional customer data (Seaborn, Matplotlib)
Compared three preprocessing pipelines for prediction accuracy
Random forest, KNN and XGBoost reached 96% accuracy
Stakeholder presentation on raising satisfaction and market share
description: Created data visualization using Seaborn and Matplotlib and performed high-level analysis for multidimensional CSV customer data; proposed and tested three preprocessing pipelines for highest prediction accuracy. Tested various ML models with Scikit-Learn, including Random Forests, KNNs, and XGBoost to develop high accuracy (96%), low error predictions and feature importances, used to draw business insights for customer acquisition. Consolidated findings into final stakeholder presentation providing personalized business suggestions to airline companies to increase customer satisfaction and capture greater market share for maximal profit.

title: To Do List App
points: MERN to-do app, built with Triton Software Engineering
Check off, edit and assign tasks to users
MongoDB Atlas backend; API calls tested with Postman
description: Associated with Triton Software Engineering. Created dynamically-updating to-do list app utilizing the MERN stack, complete with functionality to check and uncheck tasks, edit task information, and assign users. Managed backend database with MongoDB Atlas and tested API calls with Postman.

title: Bioinformatics Algos
points: Built with UC San Diego School of Medicine
Needleman–Wunsch alignment scores sequence similarity
Hidden Markov model finds mRNA coding regions
Burrows–Wheeler transform matches sampled reads to sequences
description: Associated with UC San Diego School of Medicine. Replicated the Needleman-Wunsch algorithm, inputting randomized nucleotide sequences to determine similarity. Built the Hidden Markov Model, determining the existence of mRNA coding regions through probability matrices. Developed the Burrows-Wheeler Algorithm for matching sampled reads to nucleotide sequences via data transformation.

title: Calendar App
points: Android calendar app built on Google Calendar data
Custom form to add events
Sends invites to event guests
description: Developed a working Android calendar application; app displays user data from Google Calendar plug-ins, adds calendar events using a custom-made form, and sends invites to event guests.

title: Epidemics.io
points: Epidemic simulator built during buildspace s5
Mesa and NetworkX model 500+ agents on torus grids and random networks
Spreads a user-defined infection; risk factors are agent properties
description: Associated with buildspace s5. Developed epidemiology simulator using Mesa and NetworkX Python libraries capable of handling 500+ agents in gridded torus maps and randomly-generated network models to showcase the spread of a user-defined infection. Identified key risk factors for disease spread and implemented as agent properties.
